gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Binize's 10-inch Android units, which ChatGPT picked as the cheapest at $89.99, get wireless CarPlay through the third-party ZLink app and that Binize's own spec tables mark CarPlay and Android Auto 'not for Samsung' (one Binize answer says about 85% of Samsung phones may not work), with a 1024×600 screen, while the Haudio at about $91 and the Eonon UA13 Plus at $209.99 list 1280×720 screens.
standout_why: Compared against: our current page (it lists only Eonon, ATOTO, Joying, Pioneer and Kenwood, and says nothing about Samsung, ZLink or app-based projection), pricehistory.app's Haudio page (the only rival page ChatGPT cited; it says 'Wired and Wireless Apple CarPlay & Android Auto' but not how it works or which phones fail), and howtogeek.com's budget head-unit article (it names no screen resolution, no Samsung limit and no ZLink). ChatGPT's own answers say 'verify wireless' and 'specifications on generic models deserve extra scrutiny' but never say what to check. It is not a 3 because I could not open the $89.99 Walmart Binize listing itself (Walmart showed a human check). The 'not for Samsung' line comes from Binize's sibling 10-inch Android 12 listings on binize.com. The same-name $129.99 binize.com listing only says 'Mirrorlink Yes, Both Android and iPhones'.
decides: ChatGPT's 'cheapest that clearly matches' pick, the Binize at $89.99, comes with a footnote: wireless CarPlay runs through the ZLink app, and Binize itself says Android projection is 'not for Samsung'. That rules it out for Samsung Galaxy owners, the largest US Android phone brand, and those shoppers' real cheapest choice moves to the Haudio (about $91, 1280×720, no Samsung exclusion stated) or the Eonon UA13 Plus ($209.99, 1280×720, 2-year warranty). Footnote for the table: 'Wireless Android Auto' on sub-$100 units can mean a third-party app with a phone-brand exclusion, not a built-in feature.
